DLQ coverage is solely in a `PF_DB_DSN`-gated test that skips by default, so it is not fail-able in CI; traceability claims all three ACs to this one skipping file.
AC-3 evidence absent from diff: no store-registry/ownership record and no ADR-0012 reuse/amendment shown for event delivery/DLQ ownership.
MAJOR: AC-2 requires "metrics/logs": diff emits metrics only; no log lines for delivery failure, DLQ, stale reclaim, or cross-tenant collision.

Failure isolation gap: a backing-off or non-stale 'processing' head event does `return st, nil`, halting the entire pass — head-of-line blocking up to StaleAfter (5m default) starves all later events.
Cross-tenant collision rejection (control C-2) ships with no positive/negative test in `event_dispatcher_test.go`; `UpsertSubscription` `n==0` path is untested.
Verified-backup requirement for 0026 rollback is only a SQL comment; no documented/verified backup-restore procedure accompanies the destructive down migration.

`event_subscriptions.go` adds `fmt.Errorf` with no import hunk in the diff — verify the package builds.
Confirm `EventStore.metrics` defaults to `nopEventMetrics` (or all constructors call `WithMetrics`); four new call sites in `DispatchOnce` panic if nil.
`matchesFilter` uses `fmt.Sprint` coercion (`"1"` matches numeric `1`) and re-parses JSON per subscription per event; no test for type-coercion/nested-key semantics.
Reclaimed/stale and DLQ'd-then-advanced rows are all counted/emitted as `DeliverySkipped`, muddying observability.
NIT: `StaleAfter` is an undocumented knob (no comment on semantics/ops tuning) alongside `MaxAttempts`/`BaseBackoff`.
`actionAdvance` on `failed` status increments `Skipped` rather than a distinct dedupe counter.
SUMMARY: Behavior changes (state gating, atomic cursor+delivery, cross-tenant error) are directionally right, but AC-1 test coverage and AC-3 evidence are objectively missing, and AC-2's "logs" half is unimplemented.
Top risks: skipping integration test masks DLQ proof in CI; pass-halting on retry/stale rows threatens availability; missing backup procedure for a destructive rollback.
